bottom_line: In AFIRE, rivaroxaban monotherapy was noninferior to rivaroxaban plus a single antiplatelet agent for the primary efficacy end point (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.95).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, rivaroxaban monotherapy achieved noninferior rates of the primary composite end point versus combination therapy (4.14% vs 5.75% per patient-year; hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.95) and had lower major bleeding rates (1.62% vs 2.76% per patient-year; hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.89). The document also notes early trial termination for higher all-cause death in the combination-therapy group and that early termination may overestimate efficacy data, so the magnitude of benefit should be interpreted with that caveat.

major_points.text: Multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-group trial conducted in Japan.
major_points.quote: AFIRE was a multicenter, randomized, open- label, parallel-group trial.

major_points.text: Population: atrial fibrillation with stable coronary artery disease, including those >1 year after PCI/CABG or with angiographically confirmed CAD not requiring revascularization.
major_points.quote: patients with atrial fibrillation who had undergone percutaneous coronary inter- vention (PCI) or coronary-artery bypass grafting (CABG) more than 1 year earlier or who had angiographically confirmed coronary artery disease not requiring re- vascularization

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was a composite of stroke, systemic embolism, myocardial infarction, unstable angina requiring revascularization, or death from any cause.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of stroke, systemic embolism, myocardial infarction, unstable angina requiring revascular- ization, or death from any cause

major_points.text: Primary efficacy result: event rates 4.14% vs 5.75% per patient-year; HR 0.72 (95% CI, 0.55 to 0.95); noninferiority P<0.001.
major_points.quote: event rates of 4.14% and 5.75% per patient- year, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55 to 0.95; P<0.001 for noninferiority)

major_points.text: Primary safety result: major bleeding 1.62% vs 2.76% per patient-year; HR 0.59 (95% CI, 0.39 to 0.89); P=0.01 for superiority.
major_points.quote: event rates of 1.62% and 2.76% per patient-year, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.89; P = 0.01 for superiority)

major_points.text: The trial was stopped early because of increased mortality in the combination-therapy group.

inclusion_criteria.text: Men and women who were 20 years of age or older, had received a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation and stable coronary artery disease, and were enrolled in Japan.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Men and women who were 20 years of age or older and had received a diagnosis of atrial fi- brillation and stable coronary artery disease were enrolled in Japan.

inclusion_criteria.text: Required CHADS2 score of at least 1.
inclusion_criteria.quote: The patients were required to have a score of at least 1 on the scale.

inclusion_criteria.text: History of PCI (angioplasty with or without stenting) at least 1 year before enrollment, or angiographically confirmed CAD with stenosis of ≥50% not requiring revascularization, or CABG at least 1 year before enrollment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: required to meet at least one of the following criteria: a history of PCI, including angioplasty with or without stenting, at least 1 year before enrollment; a history of angiographically confirmed coronary artery disease (with stenosis of ≥50%) not requiring revascularization; or a history of coronary-artery bypass grafting (CABG) at least 1 year before enrollment.

Key exclusion criteria were a history of stent throm- bosis, coexisting active tumor
Key exclusion criteria were a history of stent throm- bosis, coexisting active tumor, and poorly con- trolled hypertension.

analysis_methods.text: Powered to assess noninferiority of monotherapy vs combination therapy for the primary efficacy end point.
analysis_methods.quote: The trial was powered to assess the noninferior- ity of rivaroxaban monotherapy, as compared with combination therapy, for the primary efficacy end point.

analysis_methods.text: Estimated enrollment 2200 patients and at least 219 primary efficacy end points required.
analysis_methods.quote: We estimated that the enrollment of 2200 pa- tients and the occurrence of at least 219 primary efficacy end points were required.

analysis_methods.text: Primary efficacy analysis used modified intention-to-treat approach excluding patients with a technical reason for not participating.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary efficacy analysis was based on the modified intention-to-treat approach. This population included all the patients who had undergone randomization after the exclusion of patients who had a technical reason for not par- ticipating in the trial.

analysis_methods.text: Noninferiority tested with one-sided alpha 0.025 and margin 1.46.
analysis_methods.quote: We used a one-sided alpha level of 0.025 to analyze the noninferiority of rivaroxaban mono- therapy, as compared with combination therapy, with a noninferiority margin of 1.46.

analysis_methods.text: Primary safety analysis performed in safety population receiving at least one dose of trial drug.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary analy- sis of the safety end points was performed in the safety population, which included the patients who had undergone randomization and received at least one dose of a trial drug

criticisms.text: Open-label design could introduce bias, though events were adjudicated by an independent committee unaware of assignments.
criticisms.quote: The open-label design had the potential to intro- duce bias; however, all the events for which medical attention was sought were adjudicated by the members of an independent committee who were unaware of trial-group assignments.

criticisms.text: Relatively high rates of withdrawal of consent and loss to follow-up (though within anticipated discontinuation rate and consistent between groups).
criticisms.quote: There were relatively high rates of withdrawal of consent and loss of patients to follow-up.

criticisms.text: Choice of antiplatelet regimen (aspirin vs P2Y12 inhibitor) was at treating physician discretion, making it uncertain whether benefit applies equally to the two combination regimens.
criticisms.quote: The choice of antiplatelet regimen, either aspirin or a P2Y12 inhibitor, was at the discretion of the treating physicians, a factor that makes it uncertain whether the benefit of rivaroxaban monotherapy applies equally to the two combination regimens.

criticisms.text: Early termination due to increased death from any cause may overestimate efficacy data.
criticisms.quote: The early termination of the trial because of an increased risk of death from any cause in the combination-therapy group may overestimate the efficacy data.

criticisms.text: Reductions in ischemic events and death were unanticipated and may be due to chance.
criticisms.quote: The reductions in the rate of ischemic events and death from any cause with rivaroxaban mono- therapy were unanticipated and are difficult to explain on the basis of the biologic effects of antithrombotic therapy; these findings may be due to the play of chance.
